questions.q: An email arrives at sales@ from someone who is not in People. What happens?
o: A case is created and a person record is created
A case is created with no contact
No case is created - the sender surfaces in the Pulse email for a human to triage
questions.e: Auto-casing only fires for known contacts who are linked to a company. Unknown senders are triaged by a person, which is also the prompt to add them to People.

questions.q: Why do we insist on the Intact document number in the email subject?
o: It is how CRM activity and the ERP transaction record are tied together
questions.e: Intact owns money and documents; the CRM owns relationships and control. The document number in the subject is the join between the two, so a mistyped or missing number breaks the link.

questions.q: Why does that limitation matter for how you work?
o: It does not, you can always forward it
Anything important from an email body must be written into a Note
It means email is not useful
It means you should copy everyone on everything
questions.e: A Note is the only place the substance of an email can live in the CRM. Without it, the record proves a conversation happened but not what was agreed.

questions.q: Which of these is safe to change by hand on an auto-created case?
o: The link to the source email thread
The owner, next action and due date
questions.e: Owner, next action and due date are yours to set. The timestamps are stamped from real events and drive the SLA numbers, and the source-thread link is what prevents duplicate cases.
